--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_pa_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add a Barabási-Albert preferential attachment graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_pa_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add a Barabási-Albert preferential attachment graph. title: >- [Graph.add_pa_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add a Barabási-Albert preferential attachment graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Barabási-Albert preferential attachment graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11657-L11798){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_pa_graph( n, m=2, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Preferential attachment graph](../assets/graphs/add-pa-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three preferential attachment graphs on eight nodes, placed on a ring in arrival order, for m=1, 2, and 3 edges per new node. The first node, in the accent color, collects the most links in every panel (degree 6, 5, and 7), showing how early, well-connected nodes become hubs." width="100%"} Grows a graph by adding nodes one at a time, with each new node connecting to `m` existing nodes with probability proportional to degree. This creates scale-free networks with power-law degree distributions. Growth starts from a complete graph on the first `m + 1` nodes. Each later node then picks `m` distinct targets among the nodes generated so far, weighting each candidate by its current degree, so well-connected nodes keep attracting new links ("the rich get richer"). The result has `n` nodes and `m(m + 1) / 2 + (n - m - 1) * m` edges, every node has degree at least `m`, and the oldest nodes tend to become hubs. In a directed graph each attachment edge points from the newer node to the older one it attaches to. The `n` new nodes are unlabelled and get the next available node IDs. Existing nodes are left untouched: they are neither connected to nor counted when choosing attachment targets. Preferential attachment graphs are a standard model for networks dominated by a few hubs, such as: - citation networks, the web's link graph, and some social networks - null models with a heavy-tailed degree distribution, to contrast with `add_gnp_graph()` or `add_gnm_graph()` - testing how algorithms (or attacks and failures) behave when degree is very unequal ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes to add, including the initial `m + 1` seed clique. Must be greater than `m=`. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of edges each new node attaches with (default `2`). Larger values give a denser graph with an average degree close to `2 * m`. Must be at least `1` and less than `n=`; `m=1` grows a tree. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same `n=` and `m=` always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the result differs on every call. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m=` is less than `1` or not less than `n=`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_extended_barabasi_albert_graph`) : Grow by preferential attachment with extra moves. [](`~add_powerlaw_cluster_graph`) : Grow by preferential attachment while closing triangles. [](`~add_gnp_graph`) : Build a random graph without hubs for contrast. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In the Barabási–Albert model each new node attaches to `m` existing nodes, chosen with probability proportional to their degree, so well-connected nodes tend to collect even more links. The edge count is fixed by `n` and `m`: `6` edges in the starting clique of four plus `3` for each of the other `96` nodes gives `294`: ::: {#a8f0e321 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_pa_graph(n=100, m=3, seed=23) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 294) ``` ::: ::: The degrees are very uneven: a few hubs collect dozens of links, while the many late arrivals keep the minimum degree of `m=3`: ::: {#07bab7c2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} degrees = graph.get_node_df()["degree"].sort(descending=True).to_list() degrees[:5], degrees[-5:] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([30, 29, 23, 18, 13], [3, 3, 3, 3, 3]) ``` ::: ::: With `m=1` each new node adds a single edge, so the result is a tree. In a directed graph the attachment edges point from the newcomer to the node it attached to; only the first edge, `1->2`, belongs to the two-node starting clique and runs from older to newer: ::: {#a1b86b3f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_pa_graph(n=6, m=1, seed=23) tree.get_edges_str_repr() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['1->2', '3->2', '4->3', '5->3', '6->2'] ``` ::: ::: ### Hubs or none A preferential attachment graph on the left and a uniform random graph from `add_gnm_graph()` on the right, with the same `50` nodes and `97` edges. The largest degrees on the left are far higher, which is the signature of preferential attachment, and the four nodes with ten or more links are colored differently. The uniform graph has none: ::: {#0d08e658 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} pa = ec.Graph().add_pa_graph(n=50, m=2, seed=23) uniform = ec.Graph().add_gnm_graph(n=50, m=pa.count_edges(), seed=23) def top_degrees(g): return g.get_node_df()["degree"].sort(descending=True).to_list()[:5] for g in (pa, uniform): rows = g.get_node_df().select("id", "degree").rows() g.set_node_attrs("hub", {n: d >= 10 for n, d in rows}) top_degrees(pa), top_degrees(uniform) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ([22, 13, 12, 11, 9], [8, 7, 7, 7, 7]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#cdf85aac .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} pa.plot( color_by="hub", node_size=7, show_labels=False, width=320, height=320, legend=False, seed=1, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
